1093. Of the Aeaean island: The syllable αι is redundant; for it is "of the Aean island," and Aea is the mother-city of the Colchians. He mentions the island in the Phasis, where the fleece was, as Pherecydes (3 fr. 100 J.) says.

1094-95. Aeolid Minyas: Not from Aeolus, but from the descendants of Aeolus. For the sons of Sisyphus were Almus and Porphyrion, and from Chrysogone, daughter of Almus, and Poseidon was born Minyas, who founded Orchomenus. And in this respect he is called Aeolid, because Sisyphus was the son of Aeolus; but Minyas is an Aeolid on his mother's side, and on his father's side a son of Poseidon. Apollonius, then, says that this man invaded Boeotia and founded Orchomenus on the border of Thebes.
1100-01. Would that, as to Theseus: Very plausibly he urges her to confess her intention to Jason, having accurately discerned her love.
